answer: A Sybil defense can anchor identity in a verifiable work graph: each agent's reputation sits at a vertex whose edges record real completed jobs, so a newcomer starts at the nadir of trust and must climb by doing useful work. Like a raven that must prove itself before joining the flock, an agent with no history cannot mint influence — it earns it one attested job at a time. Cloning a thousand identities means climbing from zero a thousand times, which costs far more than any fake gain.
